import { useData } from "vitepress";

import type { SidebarToggleOptions } from "./inline-script.ts";
import { useSidebarVisibility } from "./useSidebarVisibility.ts";

    @click="toggle"

# Scaffolding a new plugins/* package

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `packages:` globs are per-namespace (e.g. `plugins/vite/*`,
  `plugins/pantoken/*`) — there was no `plugins/vitepress/*` entry before the
  `@pantoken/vitepress-sidebar-toggle` package. Adding a new `plugins/<namespace>/` requires adding
  its glob to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` first, or `vp install` silently succeeds without linking any
  deps into the new package (no error — just an empty/missing `node_modules` for it).
- A package that ships a raw `.vue` SFC (uncompiled, for the consumer's own Vue/Vite toolchain to
  compile) must also copy every file the SFC imports via *relative* paths (e.g. `./foo.ts`) into
  `dist/` alongside it — `vp pack`'s own bundle (`dist/index.mjs`) doesn't help here since the SFC
  is never bundled by this package's own pipeline. Forgetting this produces a
  `[@vue/compiler-sfc] Failed to resolve import source "./foo.ts"` error only surfaced in a
  *consumer's* dev server, not in this package's own `vp check`/`vp test`.
- Docs (or any workspace consumer) importing a not-yet-published workspace package needs that
  package's `dist/` actually built locally before `vp check`'s pre-commit lint hook can resolve its
  types (`TS2307: Cannot find module`) — build the dependency first if committing changes to a
  consumer that just started depending on a brand-new package.
